Computer Vision-Based basketball player training systems rely on extensive training data to detect the player's movements and poses; the current training datasets are relatively small and vary in quality, affecting the basketball training effect. This paper proposes the human skeleton detection model, basketball and basketball hoop detection model, basketball shot detection model, basketball hit detection model, and basketball hit prediction model. Intelligent technology acts as a learning assistant, providing personalized support for students and helping them learn more efficiently and independently. Improving students' writing learning effectiveness through intelligent technology has become an urgent issue that requires attention. Building upon a review of technology-assisted writing, by examining the development trend of generative artificial intelligence, this article clarifies the core essence of writing, and proposes a new human-machine collaborative writing mode. This model views writing as a fusion of artificial intelligence and human cognition, fostering mutual progress and improving both writing quality and efficiency through interactive feedback. In addition, to address the limitations of generative artificial intelligence, students need to develop high-quality questioning and guidance abilities to prevent over-reliance. Schools and teachers should also reform their teaching models, promote project-based learning and authentic writing, and strengthen students' core competencies.]]></abstract><abstract lang="english"><![CDATA[The rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the transformation of the education system, particularly posing significant challenges to the field of writing. Materials and Methods: A three-dimensional model of the right maxillary second premolar, first molar, and second molar was constructed from patient CT data. Teeth and bone were defined as rigid bodies, and periodontal ligaments were represented by axial springs. Dynamic simulations were performed with occlusal forces of 100 N and 200 N applied at three points on the occlusal surface of the first molar for 0.1 s. Displacements of each tooth and the summed ligament forces were recorded and compared. Results: The first molar exhibited the greatest displacement and ligament forces, while the second premolar showed smaller secondary responses. Changes at the second molar were negligible. The peak displacement occurred on the mesial crown of the first molar, directed toward the second premolar. Increasing occlusal force from 100 N to 200 N markedly elevated the ligament forces at the first molar, whereas changes at the second premolar remained relatively small. These findings indicate that most additional load was dissipated locally at the first molar rather than transmitted distally, suggesting a limit in the load-sharing capacity of interproximal contacts. Conclusion: Occlusal forces applied to a single molar can be transmitted to adjacent teeth through interproximal contacts, and the extent depends on loading direction and contact geometry. Clinically, establishing proper proximal contacts is essential for controlled distribution of occlusal loads and the long-term stability of the dentition.]]></abstract><abstract lang="english"><![CDATA[Purpose: This study aimed to investigate how interproximal contacts influence occlusal force transmission in the posterior maxilla using computer simulation.
